query: Original works in which copyright subsists
response:
The Copyright Act 1968 outlines the nature, duration, and ownership of copyright in original literary, dramatic, musical, and artistic works. 

Section 32(1) of Part III states that copyright subsists in an unpublished work if its author was a qualified person at the time or was such for a substantial part of the period when the work was made (if it took more than one session to complete). For published works, Section 32(2)(a) and (b) state that copyright subsists only if they were first published in Australia and their author was also a qualified person.

However, there are some exceptions as outlined by Division 5 of the Act. If a work was originally created but not initially subject to subsistence under Part III due to its publication date preceding the commencement of this Act (as per Section 210), it may still be eligible for copyright if the following conditions apply: 

- It must have been in existence prior to the commencement of the Copyright Act, 1968. 
- The work must have had copyright subsistence under the previous Copyright Act, 1911 immediately before the 1968 Act's commencement.

Section 211 clarifies that for works made or first published before this Act came into effect, these provisions apply as if references to "qualified persons" in Section 32(1) also included British subjects and those domiciled within the Queen's dominions where the Copyright Act, 1911 extended. 

Therefore, an original work is eligible for copyright subsistence under this act provided it meets the requirements outlined above regarding authorship, publication location, and prior copyright status (where applicable).
